summary.intent: Ship Phase 48 REQ-4 (share itemName lazy backfill API), then root-cause and fully fix a staging 'Decryption failed' bug that occurs after moving a file into a subfolder — including bin-restore, desktop FUSE/WinFsp paths, idempotent retry, and cross-platform e2e coverage.
summary.outcome: PR #505 (share itemName backfill endpoint + 7-step two-party e2e spec) and PR #507 (FileMetadata re-encrypt on move/restore — TS SDK, Rust FUSE, WinFsp — plus bounded desktop retry, idempotent-by-id restore, and cross-platform move-content e2e) both merged to main.

repo: FileMetadata IPNS records are AES-256-GCM encrypted with the PARENT folder's folderKey at upload; the decrypt path uses the key of whichever folder currently lists the FilePointer — so cross-folder moves without re-encryption silently corrupt read access.
The desktop FUSE/WinFsp path is a parallel Rust implementation that completely bypasses the TS SDK; fixes in packages/sdk do not protect desktop moves or deletes.

Shared-folder move is currently unimplemented — SharedFileBrowser.tsx renders ContextMenu with no onMove prop; useSharedWriteOps has no move function — so no bug exists there yet, but the first implementation must include re-encryption.

backfillSentShareItemNames fires ONLY via SDK getCoveringShares → reWrapNewItems, which is called unconditionally on every uploadFile; there is no 'sent shares list' page that triggers fetchAllSentShares — ShareDialog calls sharesControllerGetSentShares directly.
fetchAllSentShares has a 30-second in-memory cache (ensureFreshSentShares); e2e tests that depend on backfill must upload a file to trigger a cold-cache path.
Web e2e uses the built @cipherbox/sdk dist (not src); running specs against locally-modified SDK code requires pnpm build --filter @cipherbox/sdk first or the pre-fix binary runs.
Web e2e only triggers on main-push per ci config, not on PR push — must be manually dispatched with gh workflow run to validate a branch.
CI coverage (cargo llvm-cov) runs with --features fuse; all WinFsp code (#[cfg(feature = "winfsp")]) is excluded from the report entirely — missing lines there are not regressions.
CI does not gate cargo fmt or cargo clippy — only cargo test --workspace. Pre-existing fmt drift must not be swept by running cargo fmt (out-of-scope churn).
clearBytes (from @cipherbox/crypto) is the canonical in-memory zeroization helper; the project enforces clearing sensitive key material after use and CodeRabbit flags violations.

BinEntry (both TS core and Rust crates/core) use camelCase JSON serialization; Rust serde rename_all = camelCase means original_folder_key_encrypted serializes as originalFolderKeyEncrypted — compatible across the boundary.

restoreFromBin always restores to originalParentIpnsName; if that folder was deleted, requireFolder throws 'Target folder not found' before any re-key attempt — recovery requires restoring the parent folder first.
The release-please bot pushes a chore(release) commit to every PR branch shortly after PR creation; must fetch + rebase before pushing any subsequent commits.

code.finding: moveItem re-encrypt block: publish destination FIRST (add-before-remove crash safety), THEN re-encrypt FileMetadata source.folderKey → dest.folderKey, THEN publish source. Order matters: metadata is only re-keyed after destination is durably visible, so the file is always readable from a folder that still lists it under the matching key.

Idempotent-by-id guard added before the collision-rename branch: if targetFolder.children already contains a child with the same id (from a prior partial restore attempt), skip the add and go straight to re-key + bin removal. Without this, a retry after a step-5b failure double-lists the file (same id, different name) because the no-conflict publish path doesn't dedup by id.

restoreFromBin reorder: publish target folder → re-key FileMetadata (step 5b) → remove from bin (step 6). Preconditions validated before publish so a guaranteed failure (missing key, wrong type) aborts cleanly. The in-memory folderTree commit was moved to AFTER the re-key to mirror moveItem and prevent the duplicate-listing defect on retry.

New shared idempotent re-encrypt helper: if resolveFileMetadata fails to decrypt under the source key with a CryptoError, it attempts to verify the record is already readable under the destination key (duck-typed on .code discriminator) and treats that as already-done. Non-decrypt errors propagate. Shared by moveItem and restoreFromBin.

spawn_file_meta_reencrypt: bounded retry loop (5 attempts, exponential backoff 500ms–8s + jitter, lock released across sleep). Short-circuits when source_folder_key == dest_folder_key. After resolve failure, verifies the record under dest key; if readable, treats as idempotent success. Decrypt-under-neither-key is terminal (no retry).

Unix handle_rename captures reencrypt_inputs (file_meta_ipns_name, file_ipns_private_key, source folderKey, dest folderKey) BEFORE mutating folder state, then spawns spawn_file_meta_reencrypt after both folder publishes. handle_unlink captures originalFolderKeyEncrypted via ecies::wrap_key before publishing the BinEntry.

Ordering invariant test uses distinct markers per publish site: ['publish:dest', 'reencrypt', 'publish:source']. Using the same 'publish' label for both folder publishes would allow a reversed source→reencrypt→dest sequence to pass falsely.

backfillSentShareItemNames wraps the ECIES encrypt + PATCH call in try/finally that fills both plaintextNameBytes and the wrapped ciphertext buffer with zeros. Violating this pattern is flagged by CodeRabbit as a security issue.

The original code committed targetFolder.children to in-memory folderTree at step 5 BEFORE the re-key at step 5b. A throw in 5b left the pointer committed but the re-key incomplete; a retry then renamed-and-duplicated the entry because the name-collision handler saw the committed entry but the child's id was unchanged.

Added originalFolderKeyEncrypted?: string to BinEntry (placed after original_path). Captured at addToBin time by ECIES-wrapping the parent folder's folderKey with the user's public key, enabling restoreFromBin to re-encrypt FileMetadata even after the original parent folder is deleted.

workflow: Sandboxed Bash cannot reach the 1Password op-ssh-sign binary; all git commit and git rebase -S calls require dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true. Commits made in sandbox silently succeed without signatures, which causes PR merge failures on repos enforcing signed commits.

1Password SSH signer wedges with 'failed to fill whole buffer' after extended use; the only fix is restarting the 1Password desktop app. Run signed commits in the background with a timeout guard so a hang doesn't block the session.

vitest with esbuild does not perform full TypeScript type-checking — tsc --noEmit catches type errors (e.g. string | undefined passed to a string parameter) that vitest tests pass through silently. Always run tsc after writing or modifying typed code.
When running pnpm api:generate (orval), every generated file gets a version bump in its header comment — this is expected cosmetic noise, not a regression.
The gh run watch command can die on a network timeout with exit 0, falsely indicating completion. Always verify run conclusion via gh run view --json conclusion after the watcher exits.
CodeRabbit out-of-diff-range comments appear in the review body, not as inline threads — they cannot be resolved via the resolveReviewThread GraphQL mutation. Reply via a PR comment instead.

Multi-agent adversarial verification (Workflow tool, 3 independent verifiers per finding) caught a real duplicate-listing defect in restoreFromBin that passed all existing tests — the duplicate only surfaces on same-session retries after a partial failure, which the existing tests modeled with an empty target folder.

When the desktop e2e has platform-specific test sections in a .sh script, Windows runs the .ps1 equivalent — any new test section added to .sh must also be ported to .ps1, or Windows silently omits it. The better fix is a single cross-platform Node .mjs script invoked by both runners.

friction: 1Password SSH signer wedged ('failed to fill whole buffer') twice during the session, requiring a manual app restart and blocking signed commits for several minutes each time.

Sandboxed Bash silently produces unsigned commits — there is no warning, only a downstream PR merge failure. The sandbox limitation requires dangerouslyDisableSandbox for every signing operation, which itself carries prompt-approval friction.
Release-please bot pushes chore(release) commits to the PR branch after every gh pr create invocation, requiring an immediate fetch + rebase + re-sign + push cycle before further commits can land.
gh api GraphQL and REST endpoints had repeated transient network timeouts throughout the session, requiring retries with dangerouslyDisableSandbox.

The macOS Desktop E2E CI job had an explicit leniency branch that downgraded real failures to warnings — this was silently masking the unfixed Rust decrypt bug for macOS users and required careful inspection to discover.

Windows Desktop E2E ran a separate .ps1 runner that didn't include the new move-content test section (added only to the .sh), so Windows silently omitted the test and appeared green without validating the WinFsp fix.
cargo check produces dead_code warnings from the vendored fuser crate on every invocation, making it harder to spot real warnings in the output.
The web e2e stale-dist hazard (web imports built SDK, not src) is easy to forget and produces tests that validate pre-fix behavior with no indication something is wrong.
open_items: Shared-folder move is unimplemented: SharedFileBrowser renders no onMove prop; useSharedWriteOps has no move function. When implemented, must re-encrypt FileMetadata to the destination subfolder folderKey. Tracked in .planning/todos/pending/2026-06-17-shared-folder-move-must-reencrypt-file-metadata.md.

Desktop delete (handle_unlink/WinFsp cleanup) now captures the folderKey on BinEntry, but there is no desktop-delete → SDK-restore-to-a-different-folder e2e test (no restore CLI helper script exists for the desktop harness).

Idempotent clean-retry for restoreFromBin and the Rust spawn_file_meta_reencrypt is in-memory only (bounded retry, no persistent journal). A cross-session recovery mechanism (e.g. a JournalOp that survives process restart) was explicitly deferred.

The at-rest ciphertext assertion in the share-itemname-backfill.spec.ts uses GET /shares/sent hex≠plaintext as a proxy; a literal raw-bytea Postgres read (proving server never saw plaintext at the storage layer) requires adding a pg client to tests/web-e2e or a test-only debug endpoint.

sdk integration.test.ts failures require a running local API stack (docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d + pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api dev); these are always excluded from CI unit-test results but easy to misread as regressions.
WinFsp handle_rename re-encrypt added in crates/fuse/src/platform/windows/write_ops.rs cannot be compiled or locally tested on macOS; relies entirely on the Windows CI desktop-e2e job for validation.
